Course Management: Anyone can browse the public course catalog listing every PUBLISHED course, without logging in.
column3:
1. Confirm at least one PUBLISHED course exists.
2. Discard any Authorization token.
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/courses.
4. Inspect the returned list's status values.
column4: 1. 200 OK; List<CourseSummaryDTO> of PUBLISHED courses.
column5: - At least one PUBLISHED course exists.

Course Management: A logged-in learner can filter the catalog down to only their own enrolled courses, and separately search by keyword.
column3:
1. Log in as a learner with ≥1 enrollment and identify a course matching a known search keyword.
2. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/courses?filterType=ENROLLED; inspect the returned list.
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/courses?search=<keyword>; inspect the returned list.
4. Confirm each result set matches the expected filter.
column4:
1. Step 2: only courses the caller is enrolled in are returned.
2. Step 3: only courses whose title matches the keyword are returned.
column5: - Logged in learner with ≥1 enrollment; a course exists matching the search keyword.

column4:

column5: - None.

column5: - Learner enrolled before the course was hidden.

Course Management: Unenrolling using the original/parent course id after switching to a newer version incorrectly reports "not enrolled" (documented gap).

column4: 1. Step 3-4: 400 Bad Request, body {"error": "User is not enrolled in this course"} — even though the learner is still enrolled in the course family (now under id=20). Unenroll checks the raw path id, unlike enroll/switch-version which resolve to the latest-version id.
column5: - Learner switched from V1 to V2 as in COURSE_FT15.

Course Management: Switching to the newest published version succeeds and carries forward completed-lesson progress by matching lesson code or title.

column4: 1. 200 OK {"message": "Course version switched successfully"}; enrollment now points at V2; progressPercentage is recomputed against V2's lesson count, carrying forward matches by code first then by title; Enrollment.status flips to COMPLETED if recomputed progress rounds to ≥100%.
column5: - Enrolled in V1; a newer PUBLISHED V2 of the same course family exists.

Course Management: Anyone can view a course's review summary, with each reviewer's identity masked to protect privacy.
column3:
1. Identify a course with ≥1 review.
2. Discard any Authorization token.
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/courses/{id}/reviews.
4. Inspect averageRating, ratingCounts, and each review's masked email.
column4: 1. 200 OK; averageRating (1 decimal), totalRatings, ratingCounts for stars 1-5 (present even at 0), reviews[] with each reviewer's email masked: local parts ≤3 chars mask to just the FIRST character + a fixed "***" (e.g. "abc@domain" → "a***@domain", not "abc***"); longer local parts keep up to their first 6 characters then append a fixed 8-asterisk block (e.g. "johnsmith@domain" → "johnsm********@domain").
column5: - Course has ≥1 review.

Course Management: A learner who has earned a Certificate for the course (i.e. completed it) can post exactly ONE review — reviews are now one-time-only with no edit/upsert path at all.
column3:
1. Log in as a learner who has earned a Certificate for a course (completed all its lessons, triggering CertificateService.generateCertificateIfNotExists).
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/reviews body {"rating":4,"content":"Great course"}.
3. Prepare and send the SAME endpoint again (any rating) for the same course.
4. Confirm only one review row exists and inspect the second call's response.
column4:
1. Step 2: 200 OK {"message": "Review posted successfully"}; Course.averageRating/totalRatings recalculated.
2. Step 3-4: 400 Bad Request, {"error": "You can only rate this course once."} — courseRatingRepository already has a row for this (courseId, studentId) pair, so the second call is rejected outright; NO upsert/edit occurs, the original review row is untouched.
column5: - Learner has earned a Certificate for the target course (completed it).

Course Management: A learner who never enrolled in the course cannot post a review — gated purely on Certificate existence, with no separate enrollment check.
column3:
1. Log in as a learner never enrolled in a particular course (so certainly no Certificate for it).
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/reviews for that course.
3. Inspect the response status and message.
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, body {"error": "You must complete the course and receive a certificate before rating it"} — addCourseReview only checks certificateRepository.existsByUserIdAndCourseId; it never looks at Enrollment at all, so this is the SAME message as COURSE_FT21's enrolled-but-incomplete case.
column5: - Logged in learner, not enrolled in the target course.

3. Inspect the response status and message.
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, body {"error": "You must complete the course and receive a certificate before rating it"} — identical message to COURSE_FT20's never-enrolled case, since the gate is Certificate existence, not Enrollment status.
column5: - Enrolled, but no Certificate row exists yet for this user/course.

Course Management: Rating a course 3 stars or lower notifies course managers, admins, AND the course's own creator/trainer; the average crossing from above 4.0 down to 4.0-or-below fires a second, distinct notification to the same three audiences.
column3:
1. As a learner with a Certificate for the course, prepare and send POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/reviews with rating=2; confirm a low-rating notification fires.
2. Separately, arrange a course whose current average is above 4.0, then submit a new low rating (from a different Certificate-holding learner) that pulls the recalculated average down to 4.0 or below.
3. Inspect the notifications fired in both cases and their recipients.
column4:
1. Step 1: a TYPE_LOW_RATING notification is sent to course managers, admins, AND the course's creator, embedding the review text.
2. Step 2-3: an ADDITIONAL TYPE_LOW_AVERAGE_RATING notification fires to the SAME three audiences (managers, admins, creator) only because the average crossed the 4.0 threshold on this call (a rating that keeps the average already-below-4.0 without crossing does not re-fire it).
column5: - Certificate-holding learners; for step 2, a course whose current average is >4.0.

3. Inspect the response status and message.
4. Confirm Course.averageRating/totalRatings and the review row are completely unchanged.
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, body {"error": "Reviews cannot be edited or deleted once submitted"} — deleteCourseReview now unconditionally throws this for every call; nothing is ever deleted or recalculated.
column5: - A review exists on a course; caller can be its author or anyone else — the outcome is identical.

Course Management: Updating a DRAFT or REJECTED course overwrites it in place — versioning only triggers when the course's CURRENT status is PUBLISHED, never while it's still Draft/Rejected.
column3:
1. Log in as the owner of a DRAFT (or REJECTED) course with existing content.
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/trainer/courses/{id} with changed content.
3. Send the request and inspect the response's courseId.
4. Confirm the SAME course row was modified directly, with no new version row appearing.
column4: 1. 200 OK {"message": "Course updated successfully", "courseId": <same id>}; the SAME course row is modified directly; status remains DRAFT/REJECTED as applicable, no clone/new version row appears.
column5: - A DRAFT or REJECTED course, owned by the caller.

Course Management: Updating a PUBLISHED course ALWAYS creates a new DRAFT version — the version-cloning trigger in updateTrainerCourse is purely "course.status == PUBLISHED"; it is NOT gated on enrollment count at all, so even a zero-enrollment Published course is version-cloned exactly like one with active enrollments (confirmed by code read — no enrollment lookup exists anywhere in this method).
column3:
1. Publish a course owned by the caller (with or without any learner enrolled).
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/trainer/courses/{id} with changed content.
3. Send the request and inspect the response's courseId.
4. Confirm the original PUBLISHED course (and any enrollments) are untouched, and a new DRAFT row with a fresh code exists.
column4: 1. 200 OK; response courseId is a DIFFERENT (new) id than the path {id} — a new Course row is created with status=DRAFT, version incremented, parentId=original id, a fresh auto-suffixed code; the original PUBLISHED course and its enrollments (if any) are left completely untouched.
column5: - A PUBLISHED course owned by the caller; enrollment count is irrelevant to the outcome.

Course Management: Omitting the sessions field entirely on update deletes ALL existing sections and lessons for that course — a critical, high-severity gap worth verifying carefully before relying on it in other tests.
column3:
1. Create a course with 2 sections and several lessons, owned by the caller.
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/trainer/courses/{id} with a body that omits the sessions field entirely (or sends sessions:null).
3. Send the request and inspect the response.
4. Prepare and send GET on the course's detail to confirm its section/lesson count.
column4:
1. Step 3: 200 OK, no error.
2. Step 4: the course now has ZERO sections/lessons — all prior content was hard-deleted as a side effect of the missing field.
column5: - A course with existing sections/lessons, owned by the caller.

column5: - Two distinct courses with different codes exist, owned by the caller.

Feature: Submit / Publish / Approve / Reject Trainer Course

Course Management: A plain trainer's submit moves an owned DRAFT course to PENDING_APPROVAL and notifies course managers.
column3:
1. Log in as a plain TRAINER (no COURSE_MANAGER/ADMINISTRATOR role) who owns a DRAFT course.
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/trainer/courses/{id}/submit.
3. Inspect the response message.
4. Confirm the course's status and that course managers received a notification.
column4: 1. 200 OK {"message": "Course submitted for review"}; course status becomes PENDING_APPROVAL; a TYPE_COURSE_SUBMITTED notification is sent to course managers.
column5: - Plain TRAINER, owns a DRAFT course.

Course Management: A course creator who ALSO holds COURSE_MANAGER or ADMINISTRATOR self-publishes immediately on "submit", completely bypassing review (highest-priority gap in this module).
column3:
1. Log in as a user holding TRAINER + COURSE_MANAGER (or ADMINISTRATOR).
2. Create a DRAFT course under that same account.
3. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/trainer/courses/{id}/submit.
4. Inspect the response message and the course's ACTUAL persisted status.
column4: 1. 200 OK — SAME success message ({"message": "Course submitted for review"}) as COURSE_FT44 — but the course's actual status is immediately PUBLISHED (publishedAt stamped, latestVersionId updated), with NO PENDING_APPROVAL step and no notification to anyone. The response gives no indication which outcome occurred.
column5: - Caller's account holds both an authoring role and COURSE_MANAGER/ADMINISTRATOR, and is the creator of the target course.

Course Management: Submitting a course that is not currently DRAFT or REJECTED is rejected.
column3:
1. Log in as the owner of a course already in PENDING_APPROVAL or PUBLISHED status.
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/trainer/courses/{id}/submit.
3. Inspect the response status and message.
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, {"error": "Only draft or rejected courses can be submitted for review"}.
column5: - Owned course in PENDING_APPROVAL or PUBLISHED status.

Course Management: A trainer's very first course (their only distinct course code) is auto-forced to price=0/suggestedPrice=0 at the moment it's submitted for review — a previously-undocumented promotional rule that fires on submit, not on create/re-evaluate, and applies uniformly to both the plain-trainer and self-publishing-manager submit paths.
column3:
1. Log in as a trainer who has no other course besides the one being submitted (countDistinctCourseCodesByCreatorId ≤1 including it).
2. Create a Draft course and set/re-evaluate a non-zero price/suggestedPrice on it.
3. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/trainer/courses/{id}/submit.
4. Prepare and send GET on the course detail (or the trainer's own course list) to inspect price/suggestedPrice.
column4:
1. Step 3: 200 OK, same success message as COURSE_FT44/COURSE_FT45.
2. Step 4: both price AND suggestedPrice are now 0, overwriting whatever non-zero value was set beforehand — the zeroing happens regardless of whether the submit results in PENDING_APPROVAL (plain trainer) or an immediate self-publish (COURSE_FT45's manager-trainer path), since it runs before the manager/non-manager branch.
column5: - A trainer whose distinct-course-code count (including the course being submitted) is ≤1; a non-zero price/suggestedPrice was set beforehand.

Course Management: Re-evaluating price recalculates BOTH price and suggestedPrice from the tiered formula — they are always overwritten to the identical freshly-computed value; there is no separate "trainer's actual price" preserved (the request DTO has a price/priceNote field, but calculateCoursePrice unconditionally overwrites both on create/update/re-evaluate — the current UI matches this by only ever showing a read-only "System Auto-Price" value, never an editable price input).
column3:
1. Log in as the owner of a course and note its current price and suggestedPrice.
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/trainer/courses/{id}/re-evaluate-price.
3. Inspect the response message.
4. Prepare and send GET on the course detail again and compare price/suggestedPrice against step 1.
column4:
1. Step 2-3: 200 OK {"message": "Course price re-evaluated successfully"}.
2. Step 4: BOTH price and suggestedPrice have been recalculated to the SAME new value (trainerType bonus + credentials bonus + difficulty tier + lessonCount×10,000 + durationMinutes×1,000, or 0 if the creator is eligible for the first-course promotion) — price is NOT preserved from step 1, contrary to the notion of a trainer-set price surviving re-evaluation.
column5: - Owned course exists.

Feature: Publish / Reject Course (Course Manager) & Direct Publish (Trainer)

Course Management: A trainer can direct-publish their own course via the legacy endpoint with NO status precondition at all — even a fresh DRAFT that never went through review.
column3:
1. Log in as the owning, VERIFIED trainer and create a brand-new DRAFT course (do not submit it).
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/trainer/courses/{id}/publish.
3. Inspect the response message and the course's resulting status.
4. Compare this outcome against COURSE_FT50's Course-Manager path, which strictly requires PENDING_APPROVAL.
column4: 1. 200 OK {"message": "Course published successfully"}; status becomes PUBLISHED immediately — no PENDING_APPROVAL requirement, contrasting sharply with COURSE_FT50's Course-Manager path which strictly requires PENDING_APPROVAL.
column5: - Owning trainer's TrainerProfile.status = VERIFIED; a fresh, never-submitted DRAFT course.

Course Management: Trainer direct-publish is blocked if the trainer's own profile is not yet VERIFIED.
column3:
1. Log in as a trainer whose TrainerProfile.status is PENDING_VERIFICATION, owning a course.
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/trainer/courses/{id}/publish.
3. Inspect the response status and message.
4. Confirm the course's status is unchanged.
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, {"error": "Bạn cần hoàn thiện hồ sơ và được Admin phê duyệt để bắt đầu bán khóa học."}; status unchanged.
column5: - Owning trainer's TrainerProfile.status ≠ VERIFIED.

Course Management: A Course Manager can publish a course that is in PENDING_APPROVAL; every learner enrolled in a prior version of the same family is notified of the new version.
column3:
1. Submit a new-version course (parentId set to an existing published family) to PENDING_APPROVAL, ensuring ≥1 learner is enrolled in a prior version of the family.
2. Log in as COURSE_MANAGER/ADMINISTRATOR and prepare/send POST /api/v1/course-manager/courses/{id}/publish.
3. Inspect the response and the course's status/publishedAt/latestVersionId.
4. Confirm the prior-version enrollees received a notification.
column4: 1. 200 OK {"message": "Course published successfully"}; status=PUBLISHED, rejectionReason cleared, publishedAt stamped; the original/parent course's latestVersionId is updated to point at this version; every distinct learner enrolled in any prior version of the family receives a TYPE_COURSE_UPDATED notification.
column5: - COURSE_MANAGER/ADMINISTRATOR logged in; a course in PENDING_APPROVAL with parentId set and ≥1 prior-version enrollee exists.

Course Management: Course-Manager publish is strictly rejected for a course not in PENDING_APPROVAL — unlike the trainer-side direct-publish path in COURSE_FT48, which has no such gate at all.
column3:
1. Log in as COURSE_MANAGER and identify a course still in DRAFT.
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/course-manager/courses/{id}/publish for that course.
3. Inspect the response status and message.
4. Confirm the course's status is unchanged.
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, {"error": "Only courses in PENDING_APPROVAL status can be published"}; status unchanged — this is the sharpest documented divergence between the two publish paths in the system.
column5: - Target course is in DRAFT status.

Course Management: Rejecting a PENDING_APPROVAL course sets its status to REJECTED and persists the reason, which is later visible back to the trainer.
column3:
1. Log in as COURSE_MANAGER and identify a PENDING_APPROVAL course.
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/course-manager/courses/{id}/reject body {"reason":"Needs more content"}.
3. Inspect the response message.
4. Log in as the trainer and prepare/send GET /api/v1/trainer/courses to view the course's status/reason.
column4:
1. Step 2-3: 200 OK {"message": "Course rejected successfully"}; status becomes REJECTED; the creator is notified (TYPE_CONTENT_REJECTED) with the reason embedded.
2. Step 4: the trainer's own course list shows status=REJECTED and rejectionReason="Needs more content" (the reason IS persisted and surfaced, not discarded).
column5: - COURSE_MANAGER logged in; a PENDING_APPROVAL course exists.

Course Management: Rejecting without a reason is blocked by the controller before it even reaches the service layer.
column3:
1. Log in as COURSE_MANAGER and identify a PENDING_APPROVAL course.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/course-manager/courses/{id}/reject with an empty or missing "reason" field.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response status and confirm the course's status is unchanged.
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, {"error": "Rejection reason is required"}; status unchanged.
column5: - COURSE_MANAGER logged in; a PENDING_APPROVAL course exists.

Course Management: A Course Manager can hide a PUBLISHED course; hiding a course in any other status is rejected.
column3:
1. Log in as COURSE_MANAGER and identify a PUBLISHED course.
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/course-manager/courses/{id}/hide for that course; inspect the response.
3. Identify a DRAFT course and repeat the same hide call.
4. Compare both response statuses/messages.
column4:
1. Step 2: 200 OK {"message": "Course hidden successfully"}; status becomes HIDDEN.
2. Step 3-4: 400 Bad Request, {"error": "Only courses in PUBLISHED status can be hidden"}.
column5: - A PUBLISHED course and a DRAFT course both exist.

Course Management: Unhiding a HIDDEN or ARCHIVED course always results in PUBLISHED status, with no separate restore-to-archived path.
column3:
1. Log in as COURSE_MANAGER and identify a HIDDEN course.
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/course-manager/courses/{id}/unhide; inspect the resulting status.
3. Identify an ARCHIVED course and repeat the same unhide call.
4. Compare both resulting statuses.
column4: 1. Both: 200 OK {"message": "Course unhidden successfully"}; status becomes PUBLISHED in both cases, regardless of the prior state being HIDDEN or ARCHIVED.
column5: - A HIDDEN course and an ARCHIVED course both exist.

Feature: View Courses for Review / Review Detail

Course Management: A Course Manager can view the pending-review queue, both with the default status filter and with ALL.
column3:
1. Log in as COURSE_MANAGER/ADMINISTRATOR in an environment with courses in multiple statuses.
2. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/course-manager/courses/review (default status=PENDING, normalized internally to PENDING_APPROVAL); inspect the returned list.
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/course-manager/courses/review?status=ALL; inspect the returned list.
4. Confirm the default call excludes non-PENDING_APPROVAL courses and lacks full sessions[] detail.
column4:
1. Step 2: 200 OK; only PENDING_APPROVAL courses, newest first, without full sessions[] (only sectionsCount/lessonsCount).
2. Step 3-4: 200 OK; every non-deleted course regardless of status.
column5: - COURSE_MANAGER/ADMINISTRATOR logged in; courses in multiple statuses exist.

Course Management: Viewing a single course's full review detail includes its sessions[]; a missing or soft-deleted course returns 400 rather than 404 — an inconsistency vs. the learner-facing detail endpoint.
column3:
1. Log in as COURSE_MANAGER and identify a valid course.
2. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/course-manager/courses/{id}/review-detail; inspect the response for full sessions[].
3. Prepare and send the same call for a non-existent or soft-deleted course id.
4. Compare the second response's status against COURSE_FT05's 404 for the equivalent learner-facing case.
column4:
1. Step 2: 200 OK; full sessions[]/lessons tree included (contrast with the review-queue list, which omits it).
2. Step 3-4: 400 Bad Request, {"error": "Course not found with ID: <id>"} — HTTP 400, not 404, unlike CourseController's equivalent detail endpoint (COURSE_FT05) which correctly uses 404 for the same class of error.
column5: - id from step 2 unused or belongs to a soft-deleted course.

Course Management: Authoring dropdown data and public metadata lookups return only active values, and an unrecognized type returns an empty list rather than an error.
column3:
1. Log in as an eligible authoring role and prepare/send GET /api/v1/trainer/system-parameters?type=COURSE_CATEGORY; inspect the returned active parameters.
2. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/trainer/system-parameters?type=NOT_A_REAL_TYPE; inspect the response.
3. Discard the Authorization token and prepare/send GET /api/v1/metadata/categories and GET /api/v1/metadata/parameters?type=COURSE_CATEGORY.
4. Confirm both public calls succeed with no authentication.
column4:
1. Step 1: 200 OK, active parameters of that type.
2. Step 2: 200 OK, empty list — no error for an unrecognized type.
3. Step 3-4: 200 OK, public lookup data returned with no authentication required.
column5: - Logged in as an eligible authoring role for steps 1-2; step 3 needs no login.

column4:
1) TrainerCreateCourseRequestDTO.price and .priceNote carry @Min(0)/size validation but are never read by createTrainerCourse/updateTrainerCourse — price is always server-recalculated via calculateCoursePrice and priceNote is always hardcoded to "" (see COURSE_FT47). This is harmless under the CURRENT frontend, which never populates or sends either field (edit_course_page.dart's price UI is a read-only "System Auto-Price" box — see SYS_FLOW_CRS_TC03/TC04), but the DTO fields themselves are dead code that could mislead a future API consumer into thinking price is client-settable.
2) COURSE_FT44/45/59: submitTrainerCourse forces price/suggestedPrice to 0 for a trainer's first course (countDistinctCourseCodesByCreatorId ≤1), layered on TOP of calculateCoursePrice's own isEligibleForFirstCoursePromotion check already applied at create/update/re-evaluate/course-manager-publish time — two independent, overlapping "first course is free" checks with slightly different eligibility logic (blunt count-based vs. per-family code-based). Not a bug, just worth knowing both exist if either is ever changed in isolation.
